Before 2023, developers voluntarily paid $4,500 per unit under development agreements.

set.typical_award_size: Integrated Plan FY 2026-29 approved by the Board June 23, 2026 (4-0) after DHCS approval May 28, 2026 and a public hearing May 21, 2026. Statutory split is 30% Housing Interventions, 35% Full Service Partnerships and 35% Behavioral Health Services and Supports, but the County transferred 7% each from FSP and Housing Interventions into BHSS (about 23% Housing Interventions). The State approved spending up to 35% of the Housing Interventions component on capital development (above the standard 25%) for a housing development project with the Health and Human Services Agency to house HHSA and Behavioral Health clients experiencing homelessness. Dollar amounts are in the plan and budget attachments, not the staff report.
eligible_project_detail: County capital development project with HHSA for homeless behavioral health clients (up to 35% of Housing Interventions)
set.layering_notes: San Benito County is a small non-entitlement county with no housing department: the Resource Management Agency (Planning and Building, Abraham Prado, (831) 637-5313) administers the inclusionary ordinance, in-lieu fees, density bonus and TEFRA hearings; the Health and Human Services Agency (Community Services and Workforce Development) runs HHAP, the shelter and the Migrant Center; Behavioral Health holds BHSA; and the Housing Authority of the County of Santa Cruz administers vouchers and PBVs for Hollister and San Juan Bautista. The County has no HOME or CDBG entitlement, no housing trust fund NOFA and no County loan program; Hollister runs its own PLHA and CDBG programs (Pass 3). sanbenitocountyca.gov and the amlegal code library block automated access, so records were built from Board of Supervisors packets on cosb.granicus.com (attachments on d2kbkoa27fdvtw.cloudfront.net), HCD allocation tables and hacosantacruz.org. Classified as grant because the approved plan funds housing capital (a County-HHSA development project using up to 35% of Housing Interventions) and interim and permanent housing for clients. For a county of about 68,000 people the Housing Interventions share is small after the 7% transfer to BHSS; a developer's realistic entry is partnering on the County-HHSA project or an operating subsidy on a few PSH units. Source is the June 23, 2026 Board packet; the plan and budget attachments are on cloudfront via the June 23 agenda.

reason: Staff report shows a 7% transfer out of Housing Interventions and a State-approved capital development allowance for a County housing project, which the record said was absent.

set.typical_award_size: Standard state welfare exemption for low-income rental housing owned by a qualifying nonprofit or by a limited partnership whose managing general partner is a nonprofit or eligible LLC, with a BOE Organizational Clearance Certificate (and a Supplemental Clearance Certificate for limited partnerships). Claims are filed with the County Assessor on BOE-267 (first filing) or BOE-267-A (annual), with supplemental affidavit BOE-267-L (nonprofit owner) or BOE-267-L1 (limited partnership); BOE-267-H applies to elderly or handicapped housing.

set.typical_award_size: No local enhancement. The adopted and HCD-certified 2023-2031 Housing Element (Final No. 5, January 20, 2026) states the City applies California Density Bonus Law directly (described as up to 35%; current Government Code 65915 allows up to 50% or more) with incentives such as reduced parking, and offers up to a 50% bonus in the Mixed-Use District for special needs and 100% affordable projects. Program 3.8 commits to revising the local density bonus ordinance to match state law by December 2026. Financial resources: the City intends to use over $320,000 of PLHA for an ADU Amnesty Program and has passed part of its PLHA (2019 allocation, $75,999 of a $455,999 2019-2025 plan) to San Benito County for homeless services; it has no CDBG, HOME or redevelopment funds but plans to apply for competitive CDBG and holds inclusionary in-lieu fees.
set.next_deadline: No application deadline; state density bonus applies on request. Confirm whether the Program 3.8 density bonus ordinance update (due December 2026) has been adopted.
set.layering_notes: Explicit negative finding: San Juan Bautista has no local housing trust fund, no fee waiver program, no city NOFA and no city-controlled development funds beyond the Chapter 11-09 in-lieu account. Development capacity is constrained by water and sewer (a sewer force main to Hollister is a City project) and by the 8 to 15 units per acre Mixed-Use zoning; Program 3.13 commits to raising the Mixed-Use designation to 16 to 24 units per acre by December 2026. The only city-level tools are the inclusionary ordinance, state density bonus and SB 35 streamlining; capital must come from San Benito County (PLHA, HHAP, CMFA conduit bonds), Housing Authority of the County of Santa Cruz PBVs and state programs. The City's Housing Element page states the element is adopted and certified by HCD.

reason: Adopted certified Housing Element found on the City site; it moves the density bonus update to December 2026, adds a $320,000 PLHA ADU Amnesty use and a plan to seek CDBG.
